body.estimand_functional: \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=s-\prod_{c\in\mathcal C_G}(\mathcal P_c^+\cup\mathcal P_c^-)\) on the joint-margin-preserving conditional-positive-density completion family; when \(0<\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\) on every edge, the compatible-law class is the published Huntington--Klein specialization.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling within each row of a fixed-dimensional triangular array.
sampling_model.units: \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\sim P_n\), with setting indicators and the observations required for short and supershort regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Each setting has a real-valued treatment entering the partially linear causal coefficient \(\theta_i(P_n)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The residual treatment variances used by the regular map \(\Gamma\) are uniformly positive; no positivity condition is imposed on any supershort coefficient change \(d_i(\mu_n)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate the undivided primitive moment \(\mu_n\) by \(\bar h_n\), form \(\widetilde\Omega_n=\widehat\Omega_n+\lambda_n I_p\) with deterministic \(\lambda_n\downarrow0\), and map accepted primitive vectors through the componentwise polynomial sensitivity solver.  The adaptive handle uses a pilot sample to certify a safe regular cell through a calibrated sieve and an independent inference sample of size \(N\).  On a safe cell it uses numerical differences with \(\varepsilon_N\to0\) and \(\sqrt N\,\varepsilon_N\to\infty\); otherwise it uses undivided primitive-moment inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumption 3 ratio envelopes satisfying \(0<\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\), the true vector belongs to the polytope formed by the individual and pairwise difference bounds.
The conditional identified set is obtained by slicing the reported joint set at a fixed effect value.
Assumption 4 restricts bias ratios conditionally through ratios of short-minus-supershort coefficient changes.
The reported nonparametric treatment-effect bounds are the tightest possible given the observed assignment, treatment, and response distribution.
Rationalizability is equivalent to membership of observed choice probabilities in a finite generated cone.
Compatibility is characterized by finitely many inequalities and computationally efficient inclusion checks.
Calibrated projection confidence intervals control asymptotic coverage uniformly over a large class of data-generating processes.
With a Gaussian limit, ordinary bootstrap consistency requires full differentiability of the transformation.
Numerical directional differentiation yields consistent inference for directionally differentiable maps under an appropriate step-size sequence.
Joint-test inversion gives identification-robust simultaneous confidence sets for finitely many parameter ratios.
Conditional inference provides a weak-identification-robust benchmark in the presence of a functional nuisance parameter.
Observed explanatory-power restrictions yield sharp single-setting omitted-variable-bias bounds for broad causal functionals.

body.tldr: Positive bounded ratios of omitted-variable biases force one globally compatible, common-sign bias vector on each connected setting component, with the all-zero vector as a closure face.  The resulting affine product of two-polyhedron unions is the exact causal effect set on the published Huntington--Klein specialization \(0<\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\), whereas the published pairwise bias-difference polytope is generally only an outer set.  Algebraic containment continues to hold for the project-maintained generalized positive-ratio class.  Converse attainment now uses the unified construction \(A_i^B=U_i+B_iD_i\), which preserves the entire observed joint margin and proves pointwise sharpness whenever each conditional pair \((D_i,U_i)\mid X\) has an everywhere-positive density and finite second moments; nonsingular conditional-Gaussian laws are an immediate corollary.  The paper also supplies log-cycle and Farkas certificates, exact branch-linear-program and zero-safe mixed-integer computation, strict support and requested-pin gaps, and a solved three-setting cycle.  For estimated supershort calibration, undivided primitive-moment inversion is uniformly valid at exact zero, \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak denominators, and branch or basis ties.  A calibrated-sieve split-sample handle falls back to that inversion near singularities and selects numerical-delta inference on certified safe cells, giving uniform coverage and pointwise first-order recovery of the known-cell oracle at every fixed strict regular law.

project_justification.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9, imposes positive cross-setting bias ratios with intervals containing one, while Proposition 4 on p. 13 reports a polytope built from separately extremized bias differences and Definition 3 on p. 15 pins that outer set. The paper does not prove equality or converse attainment, and Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 uses divided supershort ratios without sampling inference at weak denominators.
project_justification.niche: Applied researchers need the exact joint set generated by one latent bias vector, certificates that distinguish genuine incompatibility from a numerical artifact, exact answers after several effects are pinned, and confidence sets that remain valid when the data do not identify a supershort ratio.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an if-and-only-if componentwise sign union, separates the generalized positive-ratio class from the published \(0<\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\) specialization, and proves sharpness through a joint-margin-preserving zero-safe completion under conditional positive density, with the Gaussian family as a corollary.  It adds exact primal--dual computation including fixed-zero strata, analytic support and pin gaps from the published outer polytope, and a solved three-setting cycle.  For the undivided supershort sensitivity region, primitive inversion gives uniform singularity-robust coverage, while a calibrated-sieve split-sample rule combines this fallback with numerical-delta intervals on safe regular cells and achieves pointwise first-order oracle recovery.

body.related_work: HuntingtonKlein2026 is the theorem-level identification comparator.  Its Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9 imposes bounded positive bias ratios with \(0<\ell_{jk}\le1\le u_{jk}\), and Proposition 4 on p. 13 gives membership in a pairwise bias-difference polytope.  The sharp-closure theorem proves exact componentwise sign closure and converse attainment for that published specialization under conditional positive density, while retaining universal containment for the project-maintained generalization in which intervals need not contain one.  The former nonsingular jointly Gaussian observed-law family is a strict subfamily of the attainment scope.  The support-gap and requested-pin results operate within the published specialization.  Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 motivates, but does not state, the project-maintained componentwise polynomial supershort region.  BalkePearl1997 informs the converse-attainment standard.  ChernozhukovEtAl2026 supplies the single-setting omitted-variable-bias decomposition and efficient estimation of observed sensitivity components but does not impose cross-setting ratio closure.  CinelliHazlett2020 and Oster2019 motivate the observable benchmarking primitives.  KitamuraStoye2018 and GalichonHenry2011 inform finite primal--dual compatibility and separation, not the positive-ratio sign union.  KaidoMolinariStoye2019 informs repeated feasibility inversion; the paper derives its fixed-dimensional primitive coverage and deterministic union inclusion directly.  FangSantos2019 explains the difficulty at branch and basis ties, and HongLi2018 informs numerical differentiation on regular cells.  BolducKhalafYelou2010 and Dufour1997 motivate undivided inversion near weak denominators.  AndrewsMikusheva2016 provides a weak-identification-robust adaptation benchmark; the calibrated-sieve split-sample theorem here proves uniform validity on singular sequences together with pointwise oracle recovery on strict regular cells.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Universal algebraic containment does not require a density condition, but converse attainment is proved only when each \((D_i,U_i)\mid X\) has an everywhere-positive conditional density and finite second moments.  Thus arbitrary observed laws receive an outer bound, although the covered family is strictly broader than the former nonsingular Gaussian submodel and leaves cross-setting dependence unrestricted.  The adaptive safe-cell procedure is an existence and calibrated-sieve construction: its global modulus and ball-containment certificates are not claimed to be available as turnkey computations.  Uniform coverage includes singular sequences, whereas oracle equivalence is pointwise at fixed strict regular laws.
body.honest_scope: The identification claims cover generalized-class containment, exact componentwise closure for the published Huntington--Klein ratio-envelope specialization, and joint-margin-preserving converse attainment under conditional positive density; nonsingular conditional-Gaussian laws follow as a corollary.  The paper also covers cycle and Farkas certificates, exact branch-linear-program or mixed-integer computation, symbolic support and pin gaps, and the solved three-setting equality cycle.  The supershort object is a calibrated sensitivity region, not a causal identified set.  Undivided primitive inversion supplies uniform coverage at zero and \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak denominators or ties.  The calibrated-sieve split-sample handle combines that fallback with numerical-delta inference, is uniformly valid over the stated triangular-array class, and recovers the known-cell oracle to first order at fixed strict regular laws.  The safe-cell selector is an existence construction rather than a claim of globally implementable modulus and ball-containment checks.  The zero-safe attainment identity is \(Y_i=(s_i-B_i)D_i+(U_i+B_iD_i)\) for every \(B_i\), including zero, and it leaves the complete observed vector unchanged.
